bullets: • **Pre-submission syntax validation**: Before any submission, validate that all HTML/CSS is well-formed—specifically check for unclosed comment tags (`/* ... */`), malformed closing tags, and orphaned CSS rules. Run a linter pass on style blocks and script sections to catch syntax errors before Hermes review, not after.

• **CSS maintenance: remove old rules, don't layer new ones**: When modifying existing element styles, explicitly audit the stylesheet for the old rule and delete it rather than adding a conflicting override. Duplicate selectors with conflicting values will be rejected. Example: if changing `.title-wrap h1` from red to blue, remove the old red rule entirely instead of adding a blue rule below it.

• **Validate metric definitions before implementation**: For stat cards or data-driven features, explicitly document the data source (e.g., `log.length`, `changelog` dates) and ensure each metric is semantically distinct from existing ones. Do not reuse the same data source for multiple metrics (e.g., don't assign `log.length` to both "Features Shipped" and "Stories Shipped"). This prevents redundant metrics and Hermes rejections on business logic grounds.

• **Handle zero/missing data with numeric defaults, not dashes**: When displaying numeric stats, default to `'0'` (string zero) for missing or zero-value data, never `'–'` or `'—'` or null. Explicitly code conditional checks: `value !== undefined && value !== null ? value : '0'`. This must be in both UI display logic and acceptance criteria before coding starts.

• **Match changelog entries to actual code changes**: Before marking work complete, verify that every file you modified (HTML, CSS, JS) has a corresponding changelog entry, and verify that every changelog entry reflects an actual code change in the diff. Do not document changes in the changelog that aren't reflected in the HTML/CSS/JS. This catches documentation-implementation gaps before test failures.

• **CSS insertion points must use exact anchor matching or fallback to semantic markers**: When patching CSS into a `<style>` tag, first scan the target file to confirm the exact formatting of your insertion point (whitespace, comment text, line endings). If using a comment anchor (e.g., `/* add new CSS before */`), verify it exists in the file. If the exact string doesn't match, use a semantic fallback like patching before the closing `</style>` tag instead.
